steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: Madam Extra, you must take your nutrition...

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: I said, I don't want it.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: If you have specific dietary requirements, we can make efforts to accommodate them.

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: *Sarkaz expletive*, you think I'm a picky eater?

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: Yes, you have beds and food, and your leader... that 'Matriarch' said you wouldn't do anything to me.

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: But I just don't feel comfortable.

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: In the wilderness, I know what can kill me, and I know what I need to do to give birth to this baby.

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: Where to hunt, how to keep warm, how to block off the entrance to my cave... And with that, I don't have to worry about myself or my baby.

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: But here... ugh.

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: Get out. Take the food with you. I didn't touch it. I'm sure there are people who need it more in this place.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: Reverend Gun-Knight Patrizion?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Yes. The Matriarch was looking for me?

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: She's inside. A minute, please.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: The Matriarch has been tending to the pregnant Sarkaz woman who arrived in poor shape. But it's been an hour and she hasn't come out yet...

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: I'm not one to speculate... but the prejudices of the past have made it difficult for many Sarkaz to accept our kindness.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: The Matriarch has no weapons on her. I worry that...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I'll check on her.
The gun-knight Patrizion has served Laterano for many decades. He has forgiven many Sarkaz, and slaughtered many more.
He has heard the Sarkaz curse in fury, cry out in pain, roar in hatred, even plead in despair...
But he has never heard them pray.
And yet, the pregnant Sarkaz now kneels before a holy statue, her hands clasped together, stumbling over the unfamiliar words of liturgy.
The Matriarch stands behind her, her head bowed in prayer as well, the pair bathing in the warm glow. When the Sarkaz trips over a sentence, the Matriarch waits for her.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: All mortals desire peace and happiness, and fear hardship and sorrow.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Therefore, we stand together in prayer, regardless of race.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Matriarch, the Sarkaz...

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: She has only just left behind the restless life of a wanderer. Now that she is experiencing idleness for the first time in her life, all the worries she has never had time to ponder have rushed to the surface.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: She simply needs to learn to comfort herself.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: You taught her how to pray?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: We've only recited a few verses together.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Let's go somewhere where we won't disturb her.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Why have you called me here today, Matriarch?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: I wanted to talk with you, to ease your troubles.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: But it seems like words may not be so necessary now.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Troubles? I am not troubled.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Are you not troubled, or do you dare not be troubled?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Everyone in Laterano knows that our ancient order was established in response to the prophesied calamity.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: As calamity descends, our order is stretched to its limit... yet no one can predict what will become of Laterano one day.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I cannot imagine it, but I have faith it will be beautiful.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: You have given too much for it. The granddaughter you never have time to be with, the old friend whose name you've forgotten, and the other old friends you've exiled as guardian of order...

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: To deny Laterano's future is to deny everything that you have given and sacrificed for it. It is to deny yourself.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Have no fear. A sliver of that future has already revealed itself to you.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: If the faith of Laterano can bring comfort even to the faithless, if Sarkaz can pray side-by-side with Sankta...

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Then our order shall open its arms to all.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: There will be no barriers, no one left behind, no unwilling partings.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Sounds like you're describing a dream.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Are we not about to lift the veil that separates dream from reality, before the eyes of all?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: A miracle will befall this land when everyone believes that even the most fantastical dream can become reality.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: The Nativity must go off without a hitch, Patrizion.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I'll do my best, Matriarch.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: You're blocking the screen, 'Holy Debt Collector'!

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: You're the one who decided to sit that far back... not that you're missing anything if I block a few scenes. It's just Eight-Armed Chainsaw Guy, after all.

spans.text: You're the one who decided to sit that far back... not that you're missing anything if I block a few scenes. It's just

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: And stop quoting random lines from the movie. You're not on a mission or in a briefing. You're in my house!

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I kind of like that name. Maybe you can use it as your code name for your next mission.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Not you too, Lemuen...

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: You two sure can work together, when it comes to making up bad code names.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Haha.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: How's life as a cardinal, Lemuen? Keeping busy?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Busier than when I was in a wheelchair.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: When was it that you got out of it for good, anyway? I don't remember.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You don't really care much about me, do you? I'm so sad, and the only thing that can comfort me is if you let me feel your horns.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Why don't you ask if Holy Debt Collector might let you touch her ear plumage?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Go ahead. I don't mind.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I never thought it would be the Summit of Nations that brought us back together after all this time.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: It's like every Lateran out there got called back to the city.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I can understand Legati like Mostima getting recalled, but the old man brought me back when I was in the middle of a high-priority mission to Sargon!

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Say, where is your grandpa anyway? He's the one throwing the party, right?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Should be back soon.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Who knows what he's up to? All he said was that since he was retiring, he wanted to make an important announcement while everyone's still here.
It's nice to see the kids having fun when I get home from work. Makes me feel ten years younger.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: That still makes you really old, Patrizion.

steps.name: Mostima & Lemuen
steps.text: Reverend Gun-Knight.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Now, now, are you angry at me for being late, Fia?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I had to turn the office upside-down, trying to find this thing.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: What's in the package, Reverend?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Open it. Find out for yourself.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Wow! A guardian gun?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Looks like it's been around for a while.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Patrizion. Unless my eyes deceive me...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: The first patron firearm I ever had. I picked it when I was twelve. It stayed with me for over a decade, until I became a gun-knight.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Soon, it'll become a true relic, when firearms workshops fade into the history of Laterano.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Take it, Fia.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: A little token. Think of it as fulfilling an old man's wish.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: As your mentor, your guardian, some of what I did was... how should I put it...? Regrettable.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: You know you weren't the only student I cared for. But I was never a licensed teacher. The other one should have walked a better path.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Aurela, the gun-knight who killed her cohort? That's a whole different thing.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: If I never walk that 'better path', it's not because of anything so drastic.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: It's because you don't have the little whatsis I have over my head. I know.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: But I took you in precisely because you were Liberi.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: You never told me that.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: What regret are you trying to make up for this time?

spans.text: What regret are you trying to make up for

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: *sigh*... I didn't want to tell you.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: The loss of a friendship made me realize that I never truly knew a Liberi.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I thought I was too clumsy. I thought I could learn to get along with the Liberi.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: But I was never very good at it.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I worried about your nerves that were constantly on edge, about your obsession over the accident, the anger that boiled within you, and how you struggled to fit in...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: But I never knew how to guide you.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: For the Sankta, empathy is a window that helps us understand each other. For you, it became a wall that kept you out.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Hold it, hold it right there—

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Do old people always get so sentimental?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Haha. You don't get it.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: What I'm trying to tell you is that everything is going to change after the Summit of Nations.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: The prohibition on patron firearms for non-Sankta will be lifted, along with other rules like it. The Law's acceptance of the Liberi will extend far beyond just allowing you to live in the Holy City.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: We will truly become one people, Fia.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Do you think it's enough to just issue a few edicts, close a few workshops, build a shrine, and take in some wanderers?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: See? That's your first reaction.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: It means that, deep down, you want to share true understanding with Lemuen, with Mostima... with us.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: You will understand, Fia.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Then, if you're willing, you can take my place and become a true gun-knight... or go and do whatever else you want to, things that were once open only to the Sankta.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: When that day comes, your friends will be there to bear witness, as they do now.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Now, take your guardian gun for a spin.
Fiammetta does not fully understand what the old man said, and her two friends say nothing, but everyone present smiles at her.
Fiammetta raises the old patron firearm.
She has held many grenade launchers in her time, but she feels a strange sensation come over her as she touches the gun's barrel, like a terrestrial creature touching the sea for the first time.
She cannot tell if the indescribable connection among Sanktas has opened itself to her, or if it is simply a reaction to Patrizion's words.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: We were born different, Fia, but our paths must eventually converge.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Nothing makes an old man happier than recognition from his child.
Fiammetta holds the gun tightly and lines up the sights with the door.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Fiammetta... it's been a while.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Did you invite him, Lemuen?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I knew he was coming, that's all.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: It was I who invited him.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Letting go of hatred is also part of achieving true understanding.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Is there anything I can help with, El? To make up for me not recognizing you.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Not so fast.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: There's a few things about Laterano I'm really interested in... it's been a long time since I've been here.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: When did the Curia decide to shut down every firearms workshop in the city?

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: It was recent... the edict was sent to all the workshops in the city on the same day.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: It wasn't that much of a surprise... arms control had been around for as long as I could remember, and it was about time they turned their attention to reforming gun control, after all these years.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Don't you find it strange?

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Should I?

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Magister Paganini said there was nothing unusual about shops shutting down and opening up. He'd been talking about closing up for years.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: But this is a firearms workshop!

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: D-Does that make a difference?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: This is where all Sanktas meet their guardian guns!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Have all of you forgotten the meaning a Sankta's patron firearm carries?

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: El, what are you doing?
Exusiai takes out a patron firearm and puts it on the workbench.
She smoothly disassembles it, from the magazine to the barrel to the action to the case ejector...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I'm not a terrorist, or some kind of super-mercenary. I just know my guns like I know my own joints.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I remember how I came into possession of each and every gun—yes, ALL of them.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: But the one that left the deepest impression on me was the first one, when I stepped into this little shop, along with my parents and my sister...
Exusiai's hands do not slow down even as she continues talking.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: My sister told me that every Sankta has their very own patron firearm, or guardian gun, the same as we were born with our unique halos.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: So, picking a guardian gun is like making a friend.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: We place our trust in empathy, open our hearts to one another, and learn to get along.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: You were what, four or five years-old at the time? You were tiny, didn't have a halo, and you couldn't even talk. We didn't even notice you.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: By the time we knew you were there, you had your hands on the scope I had picked, feeling it with a face full of curiosity...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Magister Paganini said he found me in the gardens of an Ecclesia Requietum, and brought me back to this workshop.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: I seem to have, er, problems with speech, and he thought I was mute at first. It took a few years for me to be able to put a few syllables together.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: I caused him so many headaches. I was never the kind of kid he could be proud of. I sneaked out that day, without even knowing why, and I was so anxious I almost cried...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Put your hand on it, Vani, just like old times.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Huh?
Hesitantly, tentatively, Vannini puts her hand on it.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Master Pag put my hand-picked parts together. My mind filled with thoughts when I held it in my hand...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Protect my parents and sister, make new friends, have the coolest graduation ceremony in Laterano... it told me I could do all that.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: You felt it, didn't you?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: The stuff you just said wasn't what I remembered at all, Vani.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I remember that I picked my guardian gun with a little girl I didn't know. We watched the fowlbeasts across the street, used the barrel as a talk tube...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: She didn't talk, but I could feel what was in her heart when we played together with the parts. That's why I knew she was happy when I saw her reddened eyes at the end.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: This is our secret. That's why I didn't say anything to my sis when she asked if I was bullying you.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: For me, that wasn't the day I made one friend. It was the day I made two.
Exusiai brandishes her gun, which she has already reassembled, and smiles at the young apprentice gunsmith.
Vannini has her eyes fixed on Exusiai, that sense of confidence and pride that was on her face throughout the process.
Vannini cannot tell where the confidence and pride came from. It is almost like Exusiai is saying, 'I'm a Sankta, and this is a Sankta thing.'

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: What is it, Vani?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Well, I basically recreated what happened... you still don't remember anything?

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: B-But I believe you, El.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Uh... huh?

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: I was really sad when Magister Paganini told me this workshop would have to close.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: I thought it was because I've lived here for so long with him that I didn't want to leave...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: I believe you about this link that you say patron firearms bring us, El... even though it means that something has happened to the Holy City that I can't comprehend.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Yeah!

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: How can I help?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: You've been here in the firearms workshop for so long. Surely you've got a way to help me make an explosion that will shake the city?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Is Fia alright?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Mostima is with her.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You know what she's like. It's not so easy for her to forgive.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: What about Andoain?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: He left.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: If there's anyone who has a right to be angry, it would be you, Lemuen. You were the one who suffered the most.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I can't argue with that, Reverend.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: But all emotions change with time.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: In the five years that I spent in that coma, Andoain served his sentence in a nomadic abbey, traveling across Terra, offering assistance to our scattered kin as his way of atoning...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Finally, he decided to come back to Laterano, reintegrating as an ordinary Nurturer.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Laterano needs him, and he deserves a second chance.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I'm glad you think that way... what was it you wanted to talk to me about?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Still Fiammetta. You know she insisted on taking firearms courses when she was in school.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: She was always the first to show up for class, and the last to leave the firing range. She loved guns in a way nobody could ever doubt... even though she never learned to use one.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: But when you gave her your gun and that speech, that look in her eyes...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I couldn't tell if it was doubt or disappointment, but the one thing I know is that it wasn't pure joy.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Is that right...? I thought she would be happy. At least, before Andoain showed up.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I still don't understand how she feels, after all these years...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Your announcement took me by surprise, let alone Fiammetta.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: 'The prohibition on patron firearms for non-Sankta will be lifted, along with other rules like it.' That part.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Yet the arms control that we've been pushing for so long has only now come to its most important stage.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: You mean the two policies conflict?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: What I want to ask is, have you received any further revelations?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Have greater goals been bestowed upon our arms control work?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: The goal has never changed. All forms of control exist so that everyone will be able to use guns more efficiently, more widely.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: The firearms workshops have a long history, but also plenty of flaws. Gunsmiths and customers both put way too much energy into them, trying to make each and every gun unique.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Once the Shrine of Gunsmithing in Pagus Michaelion starts operating for real, Laterano will be able to provide armed support to all nations and all races, when we have to.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: If the goal has never changed, why do the changes of the present seem so sudden, so... out of place?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Maybe because we're not so great at imagining the future.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: You're right that the Matriarch has bestowed a greater revelation upon me. All will partake of the same revelation at the Nativity.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: When the time comes, it won't be just you and Fia; millions of people will gain insight into the future, both inside and outside Laterano.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: You're sharp, Lemuen, and I'm sure you understand that our first priority is to make sure that the Nativity goes off without a hitch.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I will continue to hunt the criminal trying to blow things up at this important time.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Leave. Now.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I don't want to see your face.
In the end, the gathering parted on less-than-pleasant terms.
He had spent much time mulling over Patrizion's invitation before accepting it.

He was not unprepared for what might happen. But with a new dawn about to break in Laterano, he had decided to come and visit old friends, for reasons that he could not, or would not, put into clear words.
What will become of the past once the new Laterano comes?
He wanted a confirmation, nothing more.
The wind brings a cloud that casts a tiny shadow in a corner of the street. Andoain frowns.
He takes a few steps, then stops and waves over a confessional.

steps.name: Automated Confessional
steps.text: Automated Confessional CONFESS-47, at your service. Please insert your Signa Creditorum or citizen credit card before beginning your confession.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Sorry, I just remembered I have something else I need to do.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It's you.

steps.name: Nurturer A
steps.text: Is something the matter? Were you being followed?

steps.name: Nurturer A
steps.text: Was that why you waved over a confessional? To check your surroundings? Do we need to call the guards?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: No, I guess I was just imagining things.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Were you looking for me?

steps.name: Nurturer B
steps.text: The Matriarch has returned to the Shrine of Nurtury.

steps.name: Nurturer A
steps.text: We came to take you back.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Welcome back, Cardinal Lemuen.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Here are the handover documents for five firearms workshops in Pagus Faber. This one's owner, Paganini, has signed the papers.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Good work. The Notarial Hall can take the rest.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Speaking of which, there are some exceptional circumstances with the workshop on Via Borgos...

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: The owner, Paganini, has an apprentice who is going to take her qualification exam. The Curia will have to provide some form of compensation now that the shop has been shut down.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Her name is Vannini, I think. I happened to pass by her when I left... she had fiery red hair and a bright smile on her face. A really sunny disposition.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Via Borgos... sounds familiar.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Look at the files on your terminal, Amos.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: That description does not fit Vannini.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Oh—I...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It's alright. Maybe just a passerby. You said she was a Sankta with fiery red hair?

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: She had a hood up, but we were walking towards each other. I got a good look.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: (Why?)
